That truncation is common rather than exceptional - 2,248 of 4,107 stored rows (54.7%) and 479 of 1,969 product-lane rows (24.3%) were handed fewer than eight candidates, including ten of the twelve CAP-014 rows, which saw six. catalog_divergence.correlation_note:
SHORT ANSWER: divergence as such does NOT predict refutation. Only one narrow band of it does, and that band is not the band a token diff would find.

I graded all 129 items by hand on a 0-3 severity scale for divergence between the RENDERED text (name, trade_bucket, kind, description, first six support_any terms, per format_candidates_text at tools/scene_classifier_passes.py:1026-1052) and atomic_claim, scoring embed_text and require_any divergences as retrieval-side and therefore 0 on the rendering axis. Joining to Terra through analysis_debug.renovation_estimate_v5.result across the 25 readable artifacts of reports/catalog_audit_replay_corpus.json gives 907 observed_conditions with a verdict, 127 unsupported, a corpus base rate of 14.0 percent.

Pooled unsupported rate by severity band, conditions in brackets:
  sev 0, aligned          10.8 percent (18/167), 22 items
  sev 1, mild              8.1 percent (21/260), 23 items
  sev 2, material         11.9 percent (46/387), 36 items
  sev 3, strong           45.2 percent (42/93),   7 items
Binary split as usually stated: divergent (sev>=2) 18.3 percent (88/480) versus non-divergent (sev<=1) 9.1 percent (39/427). Restricted to items with n>=5 conditions: 16.7 percent (74/443) versus 7.9 percent (31/393).

Read carefully, that binary 2x looks like a finding and is not one. The relation is NOT monotone: sev 1 (8.1) is LOWER than sev 0 (10.8), and sev 2 (11.9) is 1.1 percentage points above sev 0. Terra's own same-prompt instability is 7.85 percent on the baseline arm over 331 repeats and 8.56 percent on the candidate arm over 292 (reports/catalog_audit_live_validation.json, repeat.terra_same_prompt.baseline.all.rate and .candidate.all.rate), and it flips both ways: baseline flip_pairs record supported->unsupported 11 and unsupported->supported 10. A 1.1-point gap between sev 0 and sev 2 is nothing. The entire binary effect is carried by the seven sev-3 items, which are 7 of 129 items and 93 of 907 conditions (10.3 percent) but 42 of 127 refutations (33.1 percent). Drop the sev-3 band and the "divergent" group collapses to 46/387 = 11.9 percent against 39/427 = 9.1 percent, a gap fully inside Terra noise.

The sev-3 effect itself is robust to any single item: leave-one-out pooled rates are 0.607, 0.433, 0.429, 0.414, 0.432, 0.440 and 0.458 as each of the seven is dropped, never below 41 percent. It is not one property either: the seven items' unsupported cases span 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5 and 5 distinct properties. And it is not the lexical shortcut: 130 of the 137 selections across the seven sev-3 items are resolution_path llm (paint_refresh 39/40 llm, peeling paint 88/99, and the other five 100 percent llm), so this is the model reading the rendered block, which is exactly the mechanism-B / catalog-authoring shape the assignment posed. Rank correlations over the 52 items with n>=5: Spearman(severity, rate) = 0.434, Spearman(sev>=2 binary, rate) = 0.401, Spearman(sev==3 binary, rate) = 0.491 — the strongest predictor is the top band alone, not the graded scale.

What distinguishes the sev-3 band from the sev-2 band, by inspection of the rationales rather than by the grading rule: sev 3 is where the claim and the advertisement disagree about WHICH PROPOSITION IS BEING ASSERTED, not merely how wide the subject is. Two sub-shapes account for six of the seven: (a) a disjunctive claim state whose weak limb the rendered text foregrounds and Terra silently drops — paint_refresh_recommended ('dated OR highly personalized', Terra answers only 'personalized', 12/23) and peeling_or_discolored_paint ('peeling, bubbling, OR visibly aged', Terra answers only 'peeling or bubbling', 8/37); (b) the claim naming a specific physical evidence the advertisement generalises away — unfinished_interior_wall_osb_exposed ('unfinished wall' advertised, exposed OSB asserted, 6/6), concrete_driveway_surface_wear ('wear/stained/aged' in name and embed, spalling/pitting asserted, 5/9), ornate_vintage_mirror ('dated' advertised, ornate/vintage asserted, 4/5), exterior_siding_discoloration_fading ('siding or trim' advertised, siding finish asserted, 4/10). Sev 2 by contrast is overwhelmingly bare-subject support tokens, and those turn out to be nearly free.

The clearest disconfirmations, all measured not asserted:
- wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents, the assignment's own first candidate, advertises 'stains' and carries 'stain' as a rendered support term while the claim asserts only scuffs/marks/minor dents. The divergence DOES move selection: 24 of its 188 selections are stain- or discolouration-only bullets with no scuff/mark/dent word. Terra refuted 2 of 62, 3.2 percent, the lowest of any high-volume item and a quarter of base rate.
- worn_or_stained_flooring carries the state word 'dated' on a degradation claim that asserts wear only: 145 selections, 1 of 43 refuted, 2.3 percent.
- dated_or_older_windows has six bare subject nouns and the largest shortcut surface in the catalog (96 of 131 selections shortcut): 3 of 47 refuted, 6.4 percent, below base rate.
- dated_interior_trim advertises 'dated' against a plain/builder-grade claim: 3 of 48, 6.2 percent.
- outdated_bathroom_finishes and outdated_kitchen_finishes, the two widest bare-token surfaces, refuted 0 of 14 and 0 of 15.
The assignment's second named candidate, exterior_siding_discoloration_fading, DOES hold up (4/10, and 3 of the 4 have trim, porch or masonry as their real subject). So of the two examples offered, one confirms and one refutes.

Confounds I must state alongside the numbers:
1. Terra noise, as above, ~8 percent same-prompt, bidirectional. Any item-level rate on n<10 is uninterpretable on its own; that covers 36 of the 88 items with any verdict, including four of the seven sev-3 items.
2. Terra answering the neighbouring question is not a separate error from the mechanism I am measuring — it IS the mechanism in sub-shape (a). I cannot separate "the claim was badly worded" from "Terra tested the wrong limb of a well-worded claim" with offline evidence, and I did not try.
3. Reverse causation on falsifiability: items whose claim asserts an OPPORTUNITY rather than a state are close to unfalsifiable and score low regardless of divergence — curb_appeal_upgrade 0/9, landscaping_enhancement_opportunity 0/1, dated_fireplace_surround 0/3. Several of my sev-2 items are of this kind, which depresses the sev-2 rate for a reason unrelated to divergence.
4. Selection effect from the product quarantine: the two highest-volume divergent items in the catalog, dated_lighting_fixtures (176 selections) and dated_electrical_outlets_switches (80), plus visible_electrical_risks (74), older_ceiling_fan_style (54) and dated_bathroom_vanity_light (15), produce ZERO observed_conditions and so contribute nothing to any rate. 399 of the 4,107 Pass 2d rows are therefore invisible to this measurement.
5. My severity grades are my own reviewer_interpretation. I generated candidates with a token diff and then judged each one by reading, as instructed, but a second reader would not reproduce the 0/1/2 boundaries exactly. The 3 boundary I would defend; the 1-vs-2 boundary I would not.
6. Refutation is not the only cost. wall_scuffs shows a divergence that is nearly free in Terra terms while still redirecting 24 bullets away from paint and drywall items; door_hardware_worn shows the opposite, a 57 percent refutation rate where three of the four refutations are Terra disagreeing with the photograph on bullets that state the claim exactly. Rate alone would mis-rank both.

BOTTOM LINE for the human reader: the hypothesis in the assignment is right for a small, identifiable class of items and wrong as a general rule. Divergence between what an item advertises to Pass 2d and what it asserts to Terra is common — I graded 43 of 129 items at sev>=2 — and in most of those items it costs nothing measurable. Where it does cost, it is specifically the disjunctive-claim and specific-evidence shapes, seven items carrying a third of all Terra refutations in the corpus. Any future proposal built on this evidence should be scoped to that shape rather than to divergence in general, and nothing in it should be read as a reason to reopen a recorded decision.
catalog_divergence.summary:
I graded all 129 catalog items by hand for divergence between what they ADVERTISE to Pass 2d (name, trade_bucket, kind, description, first six support_any terms) and what they ASSERT to Terra (atomic_claim subject and state), then joined 4,107 stored Pass 2d rows and 907 Terra-reviewed conditions from the 25 readable artifacts to test whether divergence predicts refutation.

Divergence is common: 43 of 129 items diverge materially or strongly on the rendering axis. It mostly costs nothing. The honest headline is that the correlation holds only for a narrow, identifiable band and fails as a general rule. Pooled unsupported rates: aligned 10.8 percent (18/167), mild 8.1 percent (21/260), material 11.9 percent (46/387), strong 45.2 percent (42/93), against a 14.0 percent corpus base rate. The relation is not monotone and the whole of the usual binary result (divergent 18.3 percent versus non-divergent 9.1 percent) is carried by seven strong items: 7 of 129 items and 10.3 percent of conditions, but 33.1 percent of all Terra refutations. Drop those seven and the gap is 11.9 versus 9.1, comfortably inside Terra's ~8 percent same-prompt instability (reports/catalog_audit_live_validation.json, repeat.terra_same_prompt, 0.0785 baseline / 0.0856 candidate, flipping both directions).

The seven strong items are not bare-subject cases. They are two specific shapes: a disjunctive claim state whose weak limb the rendered text foregrounds and Terra silently drops (paint_refresh_recommended, 12/23 refuted, every rationale answering only 'highly personalized' against 'dated paint' bullets; peeling_or_discolored_paint, 8/37, every rationale answering only 'peeling or bubbling' against 'the paint appears tired'), and a claim naming specific physical evidence that the advertisement generalises away (unfinished_interior_wall_osb_exposed 6/6, 'unfinished wall' advertised and exposed OSB asserted; concrete_driveway_surface_wear 5/9; ornate_vintage_mirror 4/5, 'reads dated' advertised and 'ornate or vintage' asserted; exterior_siding_discoloration_fading 4/10, three of four refutations with trim, porch or masonry as the real subject; vinyl_linoleum_torn_or_lifted 3/3). The effect survives leave-one-out (never below 41 percent), spans multiple properties, and is 130 of 137 selections on the LLM path rather than the shortcut, which is precisely the mechanism-B catalog-authoring shape rather than a mechanism-A shortcut artefact.

Of the two examples the assignment offered, one confirms and one refutes. exterior_siding_discoloration_fading holds up. wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents does not: it advertises 'stains' against a claim asserting only scuffs, marks and minor dents, and that divergence really does redirect 24 of its 188 selections onto stain-only bullets, yet Terra refuted just 2 of 62 conditions, 3.2 percent, a quarter of base rate. Three more high-volume divergent items behave the same way (worn_or_stained_flooring 1/43, dated_or_older_windows 3/47 despite the catalog's largest shortcut surface at 96 of 131 selections, dated_interior_trim 3/48), and the two widest bare-token surfaces, outdated_bathroom_finishes and outdated_kitchen_finishes, refuted 0 of 14 and 0 of 15.

Four ranked items bear on recorded triggers and I name the trigger and stop: paint_refresh_recommended on D6's Q-8 re-adjudication trigger; baseboard_wear_scuffs on the CAP-013 adjudication's own note about that item's embed_text (a retrieval-side divergence only, 4/33 and below base rate); popcorn_or_acoustic_ceiling_texture on CAP-016's deferred bare 'ceiling texture' token (3/25, below base rate); and window_blinds_basic_or_plain on D3, where I found a distinct rendering defect worth a human's attention — the description rendered to the model ends 'Recorded as a visible presentation detail; blinds are not billed as renovation work' (tools/issue_catalog_kind_v2.json:5035), which is a plausible rendered-text cause for the ten LLM declines D3 accepted as presentation-only. That is evidence about the cause, not a reason to reopen D3, whose recorded trigger is a frontend requirement and is untouched. I recommend no catalog edit; A-7 forbids claim-text changes and any future proposal built on this evidence should be scoped to the disjunctive-claim and specific-evidence shapes, not to divergence in general.
